name: Rissoles
subtitle: minced meat folded into pastry crescents and fried, the Anglo-Indian tea plate staple

ingredients.qty: 2, one for the dough and one for sealing

ingredients.note: beef or chicken mince works equally

prepNotes: Rissoles, croquettes and cutlets are the three fried things on every Anglo-Indian tea table. This is the pastry one.
The filling must be completely cold and quite dry before it goes near the pastry, or the seal fails in the oil.

steps.text: Rub the butter into the flour with a pinch of salt, bind with one beaten egg and a little cold water, and rest the dough 30 minutes.
Fry the onion until golden, add the mince and cook until it is dry and browned, 12 minutes.
steps.tip: Dry. Any moisture left will burst the pastry.

steps.text: Stir in the mashed potato, pepper, green chilli, coriander and vinegar. Season and cool completely.
Roll the dough thin, cut 10cm rounds, place a spoonful of filling on each and fold into a crescent.
Seal the edges with beaten egg and crimp firmly with a fork.
steps.tip: Crimp properly. A rissole that opens in the pan takes the oil with it.

steps.text: Fry in batches on medium until deep gold, about 4 minutes, and drain on paper.

storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. Crisp them in a hot oven rather than a microwave. They freeze well uncooked: fry from frozen, adding 2 minutes.
